$source: the product's own first rule about numbers: quote a figure with the conditions it was measured under and with whose it is, or do not quote it
$rule: One register of figures with the conditions each was measured under and whose it is, read by two checks. scripts/policy-sentences.py in this repository holds every figure on a shipped surface that is answered by its conditions to an entry here, and to the entry's saidWith phrase where it has one. scripts/figures-stated.mjs in the site repository holds every figure with a time unit on a served page to an entry here marked servedOnSite. A number that is not here is refused by both rather than shipping. From 2026-09-17 an entry also says what its figure is of, one of $subjects, and a sentence naming the figure as something else is refused; an entry marked superseded is refused where a sentence says it has not been replaced or quotes it as today's. From the afternoon of 2026-09-17 every entry, whatever its whose says, names evidence that carries the figure and that the check can read: a receipt in this repository whose field for the entry's subject is the figure, a file in this repository that states the figure, or, for a figure that is somebody else's, the document it is quoted from; an entry of a measurement names its owner, the machine and the path, from $owners, and a sentence giving it another is refused; an entry marked constant is refused where a sentence calls it measured; an entry marked history or superseded is refused where a sentence says it in the present. From the evening of 2026-09-17 the fields an entry is read by are structured and each comes from a closed list declared here: whose from $whose, precision from $precision, evidence as a kind from $evidence and an artefact, and, for a measurement of ours, owner from $owners and setup as $setup says. A field missing, of the wrong JSON type or holding a value outside its list is refused naming the entry, and nothing is read out of the prose of whose, conditions or evidence any more. Evidence is never a surface. The entries whose evidence still names a surface are the ones in $frozen, held by fingerprint; see its rule.
$written: 2026-09-10, in the site repository. Before it, the front page carried a made-up 12.4 ms with the conditions of a public research figure attached, and nothing would have told anybody so. Moved into this repository on 2026-09-16, so that the check on the site and the check on this repository's own surfaces read one register rather than two, and extended with every figure this repository's surfaces quote.

$whose.$rule: Whose a figure is, from this list and no other wording. An entry marked measured is a measurement of ours and carries owner and setup and evidence that is a receipt or a record; one not marked measured carries no owner, and its evidence is code where it is ours and a document where it is not. QF4 of the afternoon's set, "ours, measured", is refused here rather than read as ours.

$precision.$rule: The place a figure is written to, as "<place> <unit>" with the entry's own unit and a place from this list. Every figure of the entry is written no finer than it and at least one exactly to it, and a figure held to a receipt equals the receipt's value rounded to it: 153.9 ms is the committed receipt's 153874770 ns at 0.1 ms and is not at 0.01 ms.

$evidence.$rule: What stands behind a figure: a kind from this list and an artefact. A receipt is a file in this repository ending .cbor, .receipt or .hex, run through timewitness verify, with a provenance.json beside it naming the machine, the path, the date and the rounds in structured fields; a record is a JSON file in this repository under docs/records/ naming its figures, unit, subject, machine, path, date and rounds; code is a file in this repository holding the number, for a setting, a constant or a figure from the simulated harness, never for a measurement; a document is the title of an outside document a figure that is not ours is quoted from. None of them is a surface this check reads, a served page or this register.

kinds.receipt: a receipt committed in this repository, verified
kinds.record: a structured record committed in this repository under docs/records/
kinds.code: a code file in this repository, for a setting, a constant or the simulated harness
kinds.document: an outside document named by title, for a figure that is not ours

$setup.$rule: How a measurement of ours was taken, in fields: date as YYYY-MM-DD, and rounds as a whole number of polling rounds or a list of them for the one-shot command, or cadenceSeconds as a whole number for the resident agent, with uptimeMinutes where the entry states it. For a receipt the date is compared with its provenance record.

$frozen.$rule: The entries whose evidence still names a surface rather than an artefact, each by the sha256 of the entry as it stood on 2026-09-17 before this block existed, over every field but precision and setup. Held while it is decided whether the 23 measurements of ours among them stay published. An entry leaves this list on gaining evidence that is not a surface; nothing joins it, and an entry changed in any field the fingerprint covers is off it and refused for its surface evidence. Every one of them still carries its precision, and its setup where it is a measurement.

$subjects.$rule: What a figure in this register is of, and the words a sentence may use to say so. Every entry names one. A sentence quoting a figure is read for the nearest of these words to it in its own clause, after the figure first ("35.081 ms of the sources overlapping", whatever sits between) and otherwise the nearest before it ("the residual falls from 13.522 ms"), and that word has to be one the entry's subject is named by; nearest wins, so a sentence that puts another subject's word nearer is refused whether or not it meant the entry's. A sentence that names no subject the reader can see near the figure, and carries none of the words under neutral anywhere, is refused rather than read as agreeing: from 2026-09-18 what cannot be read is refused, because until then such a sentence passed for the same reason a forged one did. A subject named by nothing is not held to this at all: it is a setting, a condition or an illustration, and a sentence about it can call it anything but a measured part of a bound, held only where the word sits against the figure. The words under neutral are read past. Every word here and every word of a sentence is folded over the suffixes under $suffixes before the two are compared, so a form of a word is the word. Each measured subject names the receipt field it is read off, so an entry whose evidence is a receipt is held to that field and to nothing else in the receipt.

$suffixes.$rule: The closed set of suffixes a word is folded over before it is compared with a word here: one of these taken off the end where at least three letters are left, a doubled last consonant read once after -ing or -ed, so overlapped, overlapping and overlaps are overlap. The self-test refuses this register where two subjects' phrases, or two owners' words on one axis, fold alike. Until 2026-09-18 the words here were a hand-written list of forms and each cold set found the form the list lacked.

the whole interval.what: the whole width of an interval, a receipt or a reading

half the committed receipt.what: half the width of the committed receipt, either side of the reading

the sources overlapping.what: the sources overlapping, one part of a width breakdown

the model's residual.what: the model's own residual, one part of a width breakdown

the oscillator.what: the oscillator since the last exchange, one part of a width breakdown

the widest round trip.what: the widest source round trip halved, reported beside a breakdown

the local read.what: the local read, one part of a width breakdown

the safety margin.what: the fixed safety margin, one part of a width breakdown

the outside signatures gap.what: the gap two outside signatures enclose on a receipt

a ceiling.what: a ceiling a policy or a verifier sets, a setting rather than a measurement

a setting or a condition.what: a setting, a condition a measurement was taken at, an interface fixture or an illustration

a time to answer.what: how long the agent took to answer a caller

$owners.$rule: Whose a measured figure is, on two axes: the machine it was taken on and the path it was taken through. Every entry of a measurement names both. A sentence quoting the figure is read, in the figure's own clause, for the words naming each owner, and a word naming another owner on either axis refuses it, naming the entry, the word and the owner. Where nothing beside the figure names an owner, the whole sentence is read on the axis: one other owner named refuses, and two owners named refuses too, naming the axis and both, because a sentence that names two and points at neither cannot be read, and until 2026-09-18 naming a second owner bought a pass. The words are folded over $subjects.$suffixes before they are compared. Until 2026-09-17 the three most quoted figures, the committed receipt's, the agent's and the runner's, could be swapped between a desktop and a runner and between the agent and the one-shot command on every surface.
